latest_release.name: bla-agents: v3.5.7
latest_release.body:
## bla-agents 3.5.7

Optional SQLite load-time hook: when `sidecarEntangle` is on and a known safe Python loader sits beside the database, stripping the `bla.sidecar.v1` schema-comment view or a sibling sidecar fails closed at import. User tables, rows, query results, WAL/FK, and `application_id` / `user_version` stay unchanged. Default remains OFF.

### Added
- **SQLite load-time hook (`generateSidecarSqliteLoaderSnippet` / `prependSqliteSidecarLoaderHook` / `entangleSqliteLoaderWithSidecars`):** When `sidecarEntangle` is on, `protectTarget` and the `hardenProject` post-pass auto-wire a self-contained Python snippet into a same-directory loader named `loader.py`, `__init__.py`, or `__main__.py` that already mentions the `.sqlite` / `.sqlite3` / `.db` basename (`selectPythonSqliteLoader` / `discoverPythonSqliteLoader` / `isSafePythonSqliteLoader` / `isSqliteSidecarLoaderHookWired`). The hook opens the sibling database read-only at import time and, when the logical identity (`computeSqliteSidecarCodeIdentity`) matches, verifies the `bla.sidecar.v1` schema-comment view and sidecar digest — strip or sibling delete fails closed. The hook does not rewrite the database (user tables, rows, query results, WAL/FK, and `application_id` / `user_version` stay unchanged; `PRAGMA integrity_check` still holds; the existing unused `bla_sidecar_v1` WHERE 0 view remains the only SQLite mutation). Identity is a logical hash of header pragmas plus schema and stored-column values excluding the reserved view, because `DROP VIEW` is not bit-exact. Test files, already-entangled entries, and unknown helpers such as `helper.py` are never hooked. Vector `sqlite-sidecar-entangle` is recorded and defenseScore gap `sqlite-sidecar-host-verify-only` is cleared only when that hook was actually written (SQLite business-data honesty caps still apply). Default still OFF.
- **REA catalog hygiene** on tip `f8192bd39` (honesty only; no new 1:1 densify counters): REA `a2acbe393`→`f8192bd39` (+250; 213 test / 20 fix / 10 docs / 4 perf / 3 feat) added no plantable densify/budget/evidence/redaction counters and no new catalogued non-plantable limits (IDA MCP limitation strings and website/test consolidations only).

# BLA: Blind LLM Agents ### **Poison → Exhaust → Hallucinate. Make Reverse Engineering Bankrupt Again.** **The open-source Counter-REA Blue Defense MCP & CLI that protects software releases against AI reverse-engineering agents (`morluto/rea`, autonomous decompilers, and LLM recon pipelines) — verified across 14 showcase benchmark targets.** [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-bla--agents_v3.5.7-2563eb?style=for-the-badge&logo=npm&logoColor=white)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bla-agents) [![GitHub Trending](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub_Trending-%235_Daily-7c3aed?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/323569) [![MCP Server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-31_Defense_Tools-0ea5e9?style=for-the-badge)](docs/cli-and-mcp.md) [![Formats](https://img.shields.io/badge/Formats-26_Artifacts-0284c7?style=for-the-badge)](#format-coverage) [![Counter-REA](https://img.shields.io/badge/Counter--REA-Empirically_Verified-1d4ed8?style=for-the-badge)](#empirical-results-vs-real-rea) [![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-38bdf8?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE)

**[🌐 Official Website](https://bla.tools/) · [📖 Defense Guides](https://bla.tools/guides/) · [📊 Live Benchmarks](https://bla.tools/showcase/) · [🎯 CrackMe Arena](https://bla.tools/crackme/) · [🏢 Enterprise](https://bla.tools/enterprise/) · [⚖️ Disclaimer](DISCLAIMER.md)** [Quick Start](#-30-second-quick-start) · [How It Works](#-how-bla-works-agent-driven-closed-loop) · [Empirical Results](#empirical-results-vs-real-rea) · [Format Coverage](#format-coverage) · [14-Target Benchmark](#benchmark-14-targets-internal-estimates) · [CrackMe Arena](#-red-vs-blue-crackme-arena) · [FAQ](#faq)
--- > [!IMPORTANT] > **Defensive Use Only:** BLA is engineered strictly for software authors and security teams protecting **their own** intellectual property and release artifacts. See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md). > Always install from official sources: [qybaihe/bla](https://github.com/qybaihe/bla) or [`npm i bla-agents`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/bla-agents).

### 🔴 Without BLA AI reverse-engineering agents (`REA` + coding agents) unpack `.asar` archives, recover SourceMaps, trace IPC bridges, inspect `.wasm` / `.sqlite` / `.safetensors`, and clone core business logic in **seconds for ~$0.20**. ### 🛡️ With BLA (`bla harden .`) REA's default pass stops on its own resource budgets (`primitive-candidates > 256`, `ASAR > 16 MiB`, `WASM > Wabt cap`, `SQLite virtual trap`), follows realistic shadow state machines, and projects **300×–2,800× modeled token amplification** (`token-estimator.ts`). Most of those budgets can be raised by the caller — [what that means](#empirical-results-vs-real-rea). ### ⚡ Runtime-Equivalent by Design Exhaustion graphs and decoy payloads sit behind $O(1)$ number-theoretic opaque predicates ($7x^2 - 1 \neq y^2 \pmod 7$) or inert format sections. **14/14 bundled benchmark targets** pass input/output equivalence tests (`bla verify` checks Counter-REA structural gates; run your project's test suite for custom artifacts).
--- ## ⚡ 30-Second Quick Start ### 1. One-Command CLI Hardening Point BLA at any project or release directory. It auto-discovers build outputs (`dist/`, `build/`, `.asar`, `.wasm`, `.sqlite`, `.safetensors`, native binaries, Python/C/Rust/Go) and runs **audit → protect → verify**: ```bash # Node.js ^22.23.4 or >=24.0.0 recommended npx bla-agents harden . # writes a partial mirror to .bla-hardened/ — nothing ships yet npx bla-agents harden . --apply # ship it: replace the build output with the hardened files npx bla-agents harden . --restore # undo: put the original build output back ``` Build first — `harden` targets what your build produced and leaves the toolchain alone. `--apply` only overwrites build output (never source) and keeps the originals outside the project; run your own tests against the promoted build before releasing. ### 2. Agent-Driven Closed-Loop Defense (MCP + Skill) Register BLA once with your coding agent (**Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, VS Code, OpenCode, Antigravity**): ```bash npx bla-agents setup ``` Then simply prompt your coding agent: ```text Harden my software against REA ``` Your host agent automatically orchestrates BLA's MCP tools (`bla_weave_plan` → source-level logic weaving & string encryption → `bla_verify_weave` → `bla_harden` → `bla_verify`) to harden both your source architecture and compiled artifacts. Every result carries `nextSteps`, so the agent finishes the job: it asks before promoting the hardened files over the build output (`apply`), then runs your tests. ### 3. Build Bundler Plugin (Vite / Rollup / Webpack / esbuild) Protect JS chunks, strip/replace SourceMaps with VLQ v3 honey maps, and shield `.wasm` assets automatically at bundle time: ```typescript import { defineConfig } from "vite"; import { blaVitePlugin } from "bla-agents/bundler"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [blaVitePlugin({ intensity: "bankrupt", enableHoneySourceMaps: true })], }); ``` --- ## 🧠 How BLA Works: Agent-Driven Closed Loop Traditional obfuscators only rename variables (`_0x1a2b`), which modern LLMs effortlessly summarize, or wrap binaries in heavy VM packers that break cross-platform builds and degrade performance. **BLA 3.x combines format-native deterministic shields with host-agent surgical source weaving:** ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph S1["1 · Recon & Plan"] A["bla_audit / bla_lint"] --> B["bla_weave_plan"] end subgraph S2["2 · Agent Source Surgery"] B --> C["bla_encrypt_strings\n(AST Span XOR + Keystream)"] C --> D["bla_bind_scope\n(Multi-Site State Entanglement)"] D --> E["bla_verify_weave"] end subgraph S3["3 · Artifact Shielding"] E --> F["bla_harden / bla_defend\n(19+ Format Shields + Self-Seal)"] end subgraph S4["4 · Counter-REA Gate"] F --> G["bla_verify\n(Structural Counter-REA Checks Only)"] end ``` | Defense Pillar | Mechanism | Effect on AI Reverse-Engineering Agents | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Poison (Deception)** | Plants format-valid canaries, SGX/TPM2/Secure Enclave delegation manifests, VLQ v3 honey SourceMaps, and plausible shadow state machines. | Forces LLM agents to split context across conflicting hypotheses and chase synthetic rabbit holes. | | **2. Exhaust (Budget Breakers)** | Trips the analyzer's default limits (`primitive-candidates`, `alias-selections`, ASAR 16 MiB header, WASM Wabt representation, SQLite virtual column eval, Model 32-level nesting, PCAP tshark field pass (fixed 8 MiB), Electron 32 fuse sentinels). | Downgrades REA's default examination from `COMPLETE` to `LIMITED` / `CapacityError`. Where REA lets the caller raise a limit this costs the attacker a retry, not the analysis — see the last column of the [results table](#empirically-verified-on-commodity-hardware). | | **3. Entangle (Anti-Strip & Self-Seal)** | Binds sibling artifacts (JS ↔ WASM ↔ Native sidecars) via runtime SHA-256 digests (`--self-seal`, `--sidecar-entangle`) and multi-site caller scope folding (`bla_bind_scope`). | Prevents red-team agents from stripping decoys, nop-patching single-point checks, or calling exported functions as offline oracles. | | **4. Runtime Truman Show** | Hardens Electron V1 Fuses (`RunAsNode=0`, `Inspect=0`) and detects CDP / Node Inspector / Frida / WebDriver attachment (`runtime-shield.ts`). | Serves believable synthetic telemetry during live debugging while keeping normal user execution untouched. | --- ## 🔬 Empirical Results vs. Real REA These numbers come from running **real `morluto/rea`** against BLA-hardened samples on commodity hardware (`npm run redteam:rea`). Full machine-readable report: [`docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.md`](docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.md) / [`.json`](docs/redteam/empirical-rea-validation.json). > **How to read this:** “Empirically verified” means the live REA analyzer path returned the listed budget / capacity / redaction failure in this environment. It is **not** a claim about Ghidra/Frida/LLDB/Rizin/JADX sessions we did not run here. > **Most of REA's budgets are defaults the caller can raise.** As of REA `05be423` (2026-11-17) its limits are per-call inputs or settings, and REA's own error tells the agent which one to raise (`asar.max_header_bytes` up to 256 MiB, `max_interface_bytes` up to 512 MiB, `max_chunks`, `semantic_precision`). A ❌ below therefore means *REA stops here as it runs by default*: a size-based plant costs an attacker one retry, it does not lock REA out. The last column says which limits REA keeps fixed, and **JavaScript strings** is the one row measured with the budgets raised. ### Empirically Verified on Commodity Hardware Last recorded **2026-11-18** against REA `05be423` under **Node v26.12.1** (macOS arm64) with **Wabt 1.0.42** and **tshark 4.4.1**. REA analyses packet captures only on Linux / Windows, so on macOS the harness runs REA's two tshark passes, with the arguments read from REA's own provider, and hands their output to REA's parser. Soft-skips keep Node 22 / CI green when external native tools are absent; a probe that cannot call REA at all is reported as a harness error (`status: unverified`, exit 2), never as a budget hit. | Format | Before → After | REA Outcome After BLA | Exact REA Budget / Error Triggered | Can the caller raise it? | | :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Go buildinfo** | 50 KiB → 1.17 MiB | ⚠️ Rejected as malformed | `BinaryFormatFailure` — *Go build-info string range is truncated*. REA reads no build info from the hardened file, but it now checks the string range before `max_build_info_bytes` (1 MiB), the budget this plant was sized for | Not measured | | **Erlang BEAM** | 84 B → 241 KiB | ❌ Capacity error | `max_chunks` — *BEAM form exceeds the 64-chunk budget* | Yes — `max_chunks` | | **EVM bytecode** | 16 B → **4.00 MiB** | ⚠️ Admitted, just under the cap | 4,190,208 of 4,194,304 bytes of `EVM_PRODUCER_LIMIT_DEFAULTS.input_bytes`; the EVMole worker itself is not run by the harness | Yes — `producer_limits.input_bytes` | | **PCAP** | 24 B → 1.91 MiB | ❌ Budget rejected | REA asks tshark for 25 selected fields and holds that output to the 8 MiB `TSHARK_JSON_MAX_BYTES`: the hardened capture prints 12.7 MiB, so `inspect_pcap_capture` fails with a non-retryable resource error. Ten DNS responses do it — 4,076 answers each, every one naming a 251-character owner through a 2-byte compression pointer, which tshark prints in full. Without them REA read the 160 other decoys (116 KiB) | No — fixed; REA has no setting for it | | **Electron ASAR** | 607 B → **16.9 MiB** | ❌ Capacity error | `DEFAULT_ASAR_MAX_HEADER_BYTES` (16 MiB) | Yes — `asar.max_header_bytes`, up to 256 MiB | | **WASM + Wabt** | 54 B → **6.56 MiB** · 251 exports | ⚠️ `ifaceState=partial` | `max_interface_bytes` (32 MiB) — *Typed WASM interface representation exceeds max_interface_bytes* | Yes — up to 512 MiB | | **SQLite** (Node 24, `--sqlite-eval-trap`) | 12 KiB → 56 KiB | ❌ Eval trap on the honey tables | `SqliteColumnEvaluationFailure` — unknown `enclave_unseal_payload()` on virtual trap columns. Opt-in (the default through 3.4.3): it also stops the application's own `PRAGMA integrity_check` / `VACUUM`. Default hardening adds honey tables REA can read; application tables are never hidden. | Not a budget — an evaluation failure | | **JavaScript** | 761 B → 153 KiB | ❌ Budget rejected | `alias-selections` + `getter-expansion` + `primitive-bytes` + `primitive-candidates` | Yes — `semantic_precision` | | **JavaScript strings** | 340 B → 154 KiB | ✅ 0 of 3 known values in REA's result | An endpoint URL, an IPC channel and a SHA-256 digest, at 1× / 4× / 64× budgets; REA returns all three from the unhardened file. Through 3.4.3 the pieces were written in clear: REA listed the channel at its defaults and all three once the budgets were raised 4× | Raised here, to 64× | | **Safetensors** | 128 B → 9.7 KiB | ❌ Capacity error | `MODEL_JSON_NESTING` — *Safetensors JSON nesting exceeds 32 levels* (HF-loadable; tensors intact) | No — fixed at 32 | | **GGUF** | 24 B → 7.3 KiB | ❌ Capacity error | `MODEL_METADATA_NESTING` — *GGUF metadata nesting exceeds 32 array frames* | No — fixed at 32 | | **Electron fuses** | 50 KiB → 1.17 MiB | ❌ Budget rejected | `ELECTRON_FUSE_LIMITS.maximumSentinelsPerSlice` (>32) | No — fixed at 32 | | **Flutter pool** | 50 KiB → 1.17 MiB | ⚠️ Projected cap | `MAX_POOL_URIS` / `MAX_POOL_TOKENS` (REA truncates with “at least N”) | Yes — `uri_limit` / `token_limit` | Reproduce locally: ```bash export REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY=$HOME/opt/wabt-1.0.42/bin # optional npm run build && npm run redteam:rea ``` `npm run verify:rea` checks BLA's catalogue of REA limits against the same checkout (74 checks at `05be423`) and says which of them are per-call defaults.
Designed-for paths not empirically run on this machine (click to expand)
These shields exist in-tree and are covered by unit tests / catalog drift checks, but the matching REA path requires external native debuggers/decompilers not installed on the CI runner: | Area | Why Unverified Here | | :--- | :--- | | Ghidra / native decompilation depth | Requires a local Ghidra install + REA bridge | | Frida / LLDB / GDB / Rizin live sessions | Requires those debuggers + device/process attach | | JADX / full Android APK pipeline | APK resigning unsupported; standalone DEX shield is in-tree | | **Firmware** containers | Staging/extraction budgets exist; no honest E2E without firmware corpora | | **SPIR-V / CUDA fatbinary / AMD GPU objects** | Need native GPU object decoders; **PTX text** is shielded in-tree | | EVMole in-process EVM decode | Not pathable in-process; EVM shield densifies to the 4 MiB input cap | | REA's own PCAP provider (`inspect_pcap_capture`) | REA runs it only on Linux / Windows; on macOS the harness runs the same two tshark passes and REA's parser | | Raised REA budgets, other than JavaScript strings | Not measured. Every other row is REA at its default settings |

-- ''` | --- ## 🔒 Security & Configuration Defaults - **Per-Project Random Seed** — BLA automatically generates and persists a unique cryptographic seed in `.blarc` / `bla.config.json` on first run so two projects never share decoy identifiers. - **Strict Packaging Lint Gates (`bla lint`)** — Refuses `bankrupt` hardening when plaintext `FLAG{...}` secrets, single-point integrity checks, or unbound exported verifiers remain in source. - **Opt-In `--llm-directives`** — Aggressive in-band prompt decoys are **off by default**; pass `--llm-directives` (or `llmDirectives: true`) to enable. - **Opt-In Signed Attestation (`--manifest`)** — Emit `.bla-manifest.json` with `--manifest`, sign with `--sign-manifest --manifest-key `, and verify both ed25519 signature and artifact SHA-256 via `bla verify-manifest --public-key `. --- ## ❓ FAQ
Which coding agents can use BLA? Any coding agent supporting MCP or `SKILL.md` workflows. `npx bla-agents setup` auto-registers **Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, Google Antigravity, OpenCode, VS Code, and GitHub Copilot CLI**. After setup, the bundled [`blind-llm-agents` skill](.agents/skills/blind-llm-agents/SKILL.md) guides your agent through the closed-loop workflow (`bla_weave_plan` → source weave → `bla_harden` → `bla_verify`).
Does BLA slow down my app or change runtime output? No on the hot path. Exhaustion graphs sit behind $O(1)$ number-theoretic opaque predicates, and binary/model/database decoys live in inert metadata or honey tables. Every benchmark target verifies 100% input/output equivalence against the original build.
Do I need Ghidra, Hopper, IDA, or Wabt installed to protect files? No. All 26 format shields are built into `bla-agents` in pure TypeScript/Node.js. External tools (`Wabt`, `tshark`) are only used if you run the optional live REA red-team suite (`npm run redteam:rea`).
Can BLA be used to attack other people's software? No. BLA is strictly a **Blue Team defensive tool** that hardens **your own** build artifacts before release. See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).
